title: 3 months of evenings with Claude Code and Codex: my 3-minute arena PvP and raid game for Android is in closed beta
author: Revelation_X
selftext:
Gladiator's Edge: 1v1/2v2/3v3 arena fights of about 3 minutes and 4-player boss raids. Six gladiators with one fixed kit each, no gear or stats. The video is one whole real 3v3 match from the current build (Normal bots, seen from the Ranger's seat).



About me: I have some work experience in Python, but no real experience in app or game development. I designed the game, played the builds and made the calls.



How AI was used, exactly:

\- \*\*Claude Code\*\* wrote most of the code: the game in Unity 6 (C#), the headless combat simulator and its test runner, the screenshot autotests and the build tools.

\- \*\*Codex\*\* built the online play (a Cloudflare Workers server: matchmaking, parties and friends) and the Shop's billing code and tests, and drew the 13 newer skill icons.

\- \*\*ChatGPT\*\* generated the original 103 skill icons.

\- \*\*Blender\*\* is run by Python scripts that Claude Code wrote, not by hand: they build the four newest bosses and the Champion outfit props. A Python script repaints the outfits' colours too.

\- \*\*The Korean translation\*\* was made with AI.

\- \*\*Half the bosses and skill effects\*\* (and the extra cosmetic skill-effect skins): Claude Code built them mostly from the ground up, in code, to my careful, very specific direction and many example images of the art style I wanted.

\- \*\*What I started from, and what I directed:\*\* free CC0 packs: KayKit's models (the gladiators, the arena and four bosses) and Kenney's particle textures. From that base I had various outfits, weapons , and recoloured and redesigned as I saw fit. Every sound and the music are synthesized by code the AI wrote (no samples, no AI audio model), and I directed the music down to the specific drum sounds and the trance versions.



The beta is open to anyone; links and how I kept \~100k lines of AI-written code in one piece are in the comments.

comments.author: Revelation_X
comments.body:
Some context: I've played WoW arena and raids for years. Now I'm a father of two and my gaming happens in 5–10-minute breaks on my phone. But I could never satisfy that WoW arena craving I so enjoyed: kicks, CC chains, trading offensive and defensive cooldowns... So I built it, late at night after my 9-to-5: 300+ hours over 3 months, on two Max subscriptions, Claude and ChatGPT.



What made AI-written code hold together at this size (about 100k lines of C# and TypeScript):



\- \*\*The rules are a headless simulation.\*\* The combat code has no Unity in it, so it also builds into a command-line runner that plays bot duels, team fights and raids. The agents check a balance change in seconds, before the game is ever opened.

\- \*\*A rules file and design docs both agents read.\*\* [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) is the rules file both agents read every session, and it points to the design docs I wrote: a game mechanics doc, the game direction and design philosophy, one design doc per class (I handcrafted those), and a matchup doc that says how I expect every 1v1 and 2v2 matchup to play out. They give the agents hard and soft guidelines when they suggest a balance change: a tweak that breaks a matchup's win or lose condition counts as a regression, even if the win rate looks better. The rule I lean on most: bot difficulty differs by \*understanding\*, never by reaction time. A Hard bot knows your win condition and how to deny it; it doesn't react faster.

\- \*\*Autotests that look at the screen.\*\* The built game screenshots every menu at phone sizes in English and Korean and fails on overlapping text; others walk every back path and every way out of a match.



Try it (free, no ads, guest account, Android 8+; use the same Google account for all three):

1. Join the beta group: [https://groups.google.com/g/gladiators-edge-beta](https://groups.google.com/g/gladiators-edge-beta)

2. Opt in: [https://play.google.com/apps/testing/com.binarybrewery.gladiatorsedge](https://play.google.com/apps/testing/com.binarybrewery.gladiatorsedge)

3. Install: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.binarybrewery.gladiatorsedge&referrer=utm\_source%3Dreddit-aigamedev%26utm\_medium%3Dcommunity%26utm\_campaign%3Dbeta-2026-11](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.binarybrewery.gladiatorsedge&referrer=utm_source%3Dreddit-aigamedev%26utm_medium%3Dcommunity%26utm_campaign%3Dbeta-2026-11)

Which would you want a deeper write-up on: the simulator, the bot tiers, or the screenshot tests?
